abstract: We give a deterministic protocol that divides a heterogeneous cake completely and without envy among $n$ agents using $O(n^6\log n)$ Robertson--Webb queries in the worst case. Valuations may be arbitrary nonnegative, nonatomic measures, and bundles may be disconnected. The protocol makes $O(n)$ calls to certified trimming, which uses $O(n^5\log n)$ queries on $n$ pieces. In a certified trim, each agent receives the end part, or suffix, of a different piece without envy, and every shortened piece has a witness tie leading back to a whole piece. At each step, the witness values the shortened suffix exactly as much as her own. For pieces of positive interval length with strictly increasing suffix values, the retained suffix lengths are unique, although their holders may differ. Candidate assignments share a table of value and cut queries. If the coordinatewise median of their value estimates fails a matching test, the test identifies an agent whose value is underestimated, ruling out at least half the remaining assignments. A weighted median of cut marks lets one repair step remove a small envy while allocating almost all of the residue. For complete envy-free chore allocation, the query bound is $O(n^7\log n)$.
